name: JW Marriott Hotel Tashkent
insider_take: Tashkent's crown jewel sits at the crossroads of ancient Silk Road heritage and modern Central Asian luxury, where traditional Uzbek hospitality meets world-class refinement.
whats_special: This is the first JW Marriott in Central Asia, featuring stunning Islamic-inspired architecture with intricate tile work and geometric patterns. The hotel showcases authentic Uzbek craftsmanship throughout, from hand-carved wooden details to traditional suzani textiles, while offering panoramic views of the Tian Shan mountains.
pro_tip: Book a room facing west for breathtaking sunset views over the ancient city, and don't miss the hotel's signature plov (Uzbek rice pilaf) - it's prepared using a centuries-old family recipe from Samarkand.
dont_miss: The nearby Chorsu Bazaar, one of Central Asia's oldest markets, is just 10 minutes away - perfect for sampling fresh non bread and local spices. The hotel also provides exclusive access to the underground Tashkent Metro, famous for its Soviet-era marble stations that double as art galleries.
pros: Prime downtown location in Tashkent's business district
Luxury accommodations with premium amenities and services
Excellent dining options featuring international and local cuisine
Full-service spa and state-of-the-art fitness facilities
cons: Limited availability due to high demand in business district
